mapping_basis: Paper uses the Namiki name DNp09 with split line SS01540; the kit lists SS01540/DNp09 as AMBIGUOUS (DNp09;DNp71, since hemibrain 'DNp09' maps to DNp71); the Namiki-defined DNp09 (SS01540, Namiki 2018 line) supports MANC DNp09.
n_flies_note: 80 retinal-fed test flies, 72 controls (open loop); n = 50 per speed condition in closed loop
notes: Freezing was preceded by a transient increase in walking speed ('running') in flies that were mostly already walking (Fig. 6d, baseline ~11 mm/s), and jumps occurred at light offset. Coded per the stopping convention (legs 'no', stops); the transient running is listed as a secondary behaviour. Freezing scored by a pixel-change classifier, not leg tracking. Closed-loop speed-dependent stimulation (Fig. 6g) gives the same outcome class with different probability, so it is folded into this record.
other_cell_types: weak off-target labeling (cells not named in the paper; see FlyLight SS01540)
penetrance: freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of stimulation trials; closed-loop: 85% (506/593) at low speed, 55% (223/403) at very high speed
quote: We found that CsChrimson activation of DNp09 neurons was sufficient to trigger freezing in 61.5% (492/800) of trials
sensory_condition: freely moving in 30 mm closed arena, IR backlight; controls raised without retinal
source_locator: Results 'Activation of DNp09 neurons induced freezing'; Fig. 6b-g; Methods 'Optogenetic activation'
stimulation: 627 nm LEDs, total 0.025 mW/mm2; 10 x (2 s on, 20 s off); also closed-loop triggering at low/high/very high walking speed (Fig. 6g)
title: Speed dependent descending control of freezing behavior in Drosophila melanogaster.
